mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses equity discount rates by reducing risk-free rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors shift capital from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for two consecutive months signals labor market deterioration, prompting central bank rate cuts that boost S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline of HOUST and RSAFS shows no negative correlation with SPX 5-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), rising federal funds rates signal aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY periods, 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases despite rising FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 indicates manufacturing sector weakness, which typically precedes equity market declines, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO remains below 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) falling below 500.0 thousand units for two months signals housing market contraction, reducing consumer confidence and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST remains below 500.0 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Joint decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates severe labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE shows no negative correlation with SPX 5-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% YoY), a slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1 < 1.5% YoY) signals economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 YoY growth > 2.5%), 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases when GDPC1 growth slows below 1.5% YoY.
